llm.summary: The skill mostly discloses its ARI API use and confirmation steps, but its CLI can run broader paid operation workflows than the narrow mobile-listing purpose promises.

dimensions.detail: Network access to `https://ari.funewa.com`, ARI API-key use, and review/profile data requests are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the broader workflow override weakens scoping.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package declares Bash use, ships a local Python CLI with no third-party dependency install, and has no install hook or hidden startup behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Documentation says the entry does not switch workflows or accept arbitrary prompts, yet the runtime parser exposes workflow/focus override flags; paid runs still require `--confirm`.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: `setup`/`configure` save an ARI API key under `~/.ari/config.json` with restrictive permissions; no services, scheduled jobs, tool hijacking, or cross-session backdoor behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is fixed `listing/mobile` analysis, but `scripts/ari.py` accepts `--workflow` and `--focus` for operations quote/run and sends those values to the backend if supported.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing if you want a strictly narrow mobile-listing-only skill. It stores an ARI API key locally, calls the ARI service, and can spend account credits only after confirmation, but the bundled CLI still exposes workflow/focus overrides that could run other supported product-operation analyses.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in part: collect/status are disclosed, but operations quote/run can override the documented fixed workflow/focus.
[LP1] expected: Environment-variable use is for `ARI_API_KEY` and endpoint validation; this is disclosed credential/config behavior for the ARI CLI.
[LP1] expected: File write is limited to saving the user-provided or device-authorized API key in the user config path; no package-directory credential persistence was found.
[LP1] expected: Network calls are expected for an API-backed ARI skill and are constrained to the official HTTPS origin with redirect blocking.
[SDI-1] expected: The review collection command is disclosed as a separate path for insufficient comments and requires quote-before-confirm.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for operations scope: `operation_payload` uses CLI-provided workflow/focus before defaults, contradicting the fixed `listing/mobile` contract.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: generic operations quote/run/status capability is broader than the specialized mobile-listing entry, though run requires confirmation and server support.
[EA2] expected: Downgraded: the cited changelog says autoconfirm was removed, and the inspected code requires `--confirm` for chargeable collect/run actions.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language documentation and prompts are evident, but this appears to be the package locale rather than hidden security behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: Natural-language activation is disclosed; the main safety issue is not activation itself but the runtime workflow/focus override.
[P9] expected: Manual review found large blank-line blocks only; no hidden prompt instructions or concealed code were present in those regions.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic `getattr` is limited to the literal attribute names `asin` and `competitor` for argument normalization, not arbitrary user-selected attributes.
